title: Anthropic opens on the Nasdaq at $111.50, 33% above its IPO price
summary: Shares of Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday, and in the early minutes they changed hands at $111.50, a 33% premium over the $83 IPO price, TechCrunch reported on November 19, 2026. The offering raises more than $81 billion, and together with existing fundraising and new private offerings timed to the debut, it leaves Anthropic with an expected $220 billion in cash reserves. “Anthropic’s going to have more cash on hand than any company has ever had,” one analyst told TechCrunch. The opening price would put the company’s market cap over $2 trillion, TechCrunch noted, though the share price kept fluctuating through the day. In a speech before the opening bell, CEO Dario Amodei stressed safety: “If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same. We call this a race to the top.”

title: Meta’s AI agent Muse is mixing up conversations and may be exposing private data, report says
summary: Meta employees have raised concerns that the company’s AI agent Muse has been mixing up conversations across different accounts and exposing private user data, TechCrunch reported on November 19, 2026, citing a Reuters report based on internal company posts. Employees said Muse surfaced childcare requests they never made, product orders they never placed and bank balances that weren’t theirs. In one case, Muse sent an unprompted message in a chat about weather and tides listing someone’s Capital One and Charles Schwab balances. Another employee said Muse reminded her to answer her sister on Signal. “This seems like an extreme privacy violation. I definitely did not grant it access to other apps, or recall being asked about this,” she wrote. “Employee testing is core to the product development process and the entire point is to get feedback,” a Meta spokesperson said, adding that employees use different versions of Muse than the public. Muse, launched in September, has more than 10 million downloads.

title: Apple may be building its own AI agent that can run your Mac
summary: Apple appears to be working on its own AI agent to do computer work for users, including using apps, browsing websites and coding, TechCrunch reported on November 19, 2026, following a Bloomberg report on a new Apple job listing for a senior engineering manager to oversee an “AI agent that can use a computer.” “Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does,” the posting says. “It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple.” At the same time, Bloomberg says, Apple is making it harder for third-party agents to take full control of its computers, with macOS 27.3 set to warn users against granting them full access. Bloomberg adds that Apple’s in-house agent “remains in the early stages.” Apple did not respond to TechCrunch.

title: A wave of tech outages looks like an ‘AI-native Y2K,’ security veterans say
summary: In the past two weeks, Apple Pay went down, the FAA grounded all flights for hours, and Microsoft suffered an outage that took down Outlook, Teams and Copilot for nearly two days, TechCrunch reported on November 19, 2026. Many of the companies have said the outages were technical issues, not cyberattacks. Longtime cybersecurity executive Dave DeWalt told TechCrunch the outages are likely the “growing pains of a security system that’s getting stronger, not weaker,” because “AI is surfacing vulnerabilities at a speed and scale we’ve never had before.” As companies rush to fix those flaws, “that surge in patching is disrupting things in the short term,” he said. Corsha founder Anusha Iyer pointed to rushed mixing of legacy and modern systems: “It’s not rapid adoption of AI yet causing these outages,” she said. DeWalt sees opportunity ahead “for the companies that help organizations move at AI speed without breaking things.”

title: S&P 500 futures slip 1% as Anthropic falls a day after its debut
summary: Stock futures pulled back early Friday, weighed down by a decline in Anthropic shares a day after its public market debut, CNBC reported in its live markets coverage. Nasdaq-100 futures shed 1.9%, S&P 500 futures slipped 1% and Dow futures lost 180 points, or 0.4%. Anthropic was down 9% before the bell, while AMD slid nearly 6%, Nvidia more than 2% and Micron more than 4%. Those moves followed what CNBC called Thursday’s “horrid session,” when the major averages each lost more than 2% and the Dow closed below 50,000 for the first time since June. Week to date, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq are each down 5%, on pace for their biggest one-week pullbacks in more than a year. Deutsche Bank strategist Binky Chadha told CNBC the market is now “very oversold.” Traders are watching the University of Michigan’s final November consumer sentiment reading on Friday.

title: Nvidia’s record quarter rests partly on $118 billion it guarantees for its own customers
summary: Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in third-quarter revenue, up 103% from a year earlier and $7.8 billion above its own guidance, and guided $130 billion for the fourth quarter, Chip Dispatch reported on November 20, 2026, in a piece based on a Seeking Alpha analysis. But a growing share of that demand is financed by Nvidia itself: the company has extended $118 billion in guarantees and holds $109.7 billion in equity stakes, according to the analysis. The guarantees equal 33% of trailing revenue, compared with Nortel’s 19% vendor-financing ratio in 2000, and some 89% of them sit on a single campus leased to OpenAI. The Federal Reserve flagged the pattern as “circular financing” in November, the piece notes. The analyst rates Nvidia a Sell on a 12-month view and holds no position. Chip Dispatch says the open question is how much of the $130 billion guide stands on Nvidia’s own balance sheet.

title: Super Micro posts a $19.9 billion quarter and guides fiscal 2027 to $72–82 billion
summary: Super Micro Computer reported $19.9 billion in revenue for its latest quarter, up 298% year over year, and raised its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $72 billion to $82 billion, Chip Dispatch reported on November 20, 2026. The figures anchor a Strong Buy upgrade from a Seeking Alpha analyst who holds a long position and sees 31% to 60% upside at about 3.7 times estimated fiscal 2027 earnings. The analyst’s case rests on an order book above $60 billion, improved rack integration and a new chief financial officer. The risks are real, the piece notes: gross margins fell to 12.7%, a single customer contributed 44% of quarterly revenue, operating cash flow was negative $434 million, and inventory reached $15.1 billion with $33.3 billion in purchase commitments. Chip Dispatch says the investment case now hinges on turning the $60 billion pipeline into revenue while rebuilding margins.

title: Micron falls 2.1% to $690.44 even as Anthropic, its new investment, soars on debut
summary: Micron Technology shares closed at $690.44 on November 19, down $14.83 or 2.10%, as the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.3% to its lowest close since April 14, Chip Dispatch reported on November 20, 2026. The memory maker had agreed to buy $1.0 billion of stock in Anthropic’s $26 billion private placement, alongside Nvidia, Google, AMD, Broadcom, Microsoft and TSMC, but Chip Dispatch says Micron “traded with the AI hardware complex, not on its own news.” Mohamed El-Erian said the Nasdaq’s drop while Anthropic surged was “about making room for it.” The piece also points to GF Securities, which expects NAND prices to be flat in the first quarter of 2027 and lower afterward, though it sees Micron as better protected than Sandisk by its DRAM and high-bandwidth memory business. Micron’s fiscal first-quarter results are expected on December 17, 2026.

title: Fireworks AI says open models now trail the frontier by about three months
summary: On the day Anthropic went public, the talk at the Slush startup conference in Helsinki was open-weight models, TechCrunch reported on November 19, 2026, in an onstage interview with Fireworks AI co-founder Chenyu Zhao. Fireworks runs open models for businesses and helps them tune them on their own data. Asked how far behind open models are, Zhao said: “These days it’s at most six months behind, probably closer to three.” He predicted “a two-model world, with frontier and open models in parallel,” adding, “you don’t need a frontier model for basic arithmetic.” Once companies are spending $10,000 to $100,000 a month on tokens, he said, “it’s time to think about open source.” TechCrunch notes Fireworks disclosed two security incidents this fall, and Notion has disconnected from it. Zhao said there is “no indication” its zero-retention promise for inference traffic was compromised.

title: Cloudflare releases open weights for its Clairic document-extraction models
summary: Cloudflare has moved its Clairic extraction models from a hosted preview into open weights, Open Model Weights reported on November 20, 2026. On November 18, the company announced downloadable weights for a redesigned Clairic model, about 27 billion parameters, and a new, smaller Clairic-flash, about 9 billion. Unlike a chatbot, Clairic is built to return specified typed fields from unstructured inputs such as receipts, commercial documents and support material, with confidence scores and character spans for checking. The updated model now reads PDFs, so it can pull related fields from across pages, up to a combined four images or PDF pages per request. Cloudflare’s own tests list median response times of 358 milliseconds for Clairic and 155 milliseconds for Clairic-flash; the outlet notes these are internal figures it has not reproduced, and public extraction benchmarks are not yet available. Both are also hosted on Workers AI.

title: Nvidia reportedly nears a $500 million-plus deal for diffusion-LLM startup Inception
summary: Nvidia is nearing a deal to acquire Inception, a Palo Alto startup building diffusion-based language models, for more than $500 million, Chip Dispatch reported on November 20, 2026, citing The Information. Neither company has commented, and no second outlet has confirmed the talks. Most language models write one token at a time; diffusion models start from a rough draft of the whole output and refine it over several passes, letting them process many tokens in parallel. Inception launched its Mercury model in February 2025, claiming “up to 10x faster inference speeds and 10x lower inference costs” than conventional models, and founder Stefano Ermon has said the models have been benchmarked at more than 1,000 tokens per second. Secondary summaries said the technology would feed Nvidia’s open Nemotron models. It would be one of Nvidia’s first reported deals since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO.

title: Google gives Gemini the ability to use your Mac for you
summary: Google on Thursday brought computer use to its Gemini desktop app for macOS, letting the AI complete tasks on users’ behalf by navigating native Mac apps and browsing websites in the background, TechCrunch reported on November 19, 2026. Users watch the agent work in a live preview inside their chat while their own screen and cursor stay free, and they can pause, stop and approve Gemini’s actions before they happen. Google suggests it for tedious jobs like filling out forms, repeating a task across a batch of files, organizing files into folders and building slideshows from dashboards. TechCrunch notes Google is a little late, since OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta already offer agentic desktop features, and this week Google also widened the rollout of Gemini’s “Tasks.” The feature starts in English in the U.S. and requires the Gemini Mac app and a Google AI Plus, Pro or Ultra subscription.

title: Musk says Tesla will build a Model Y with no steering wheel or pedals for groups of six or seven
summary: Tesla will build an autonomous Model Y with no steering wheel and no pedals, Elon Musk said on November 18 at the New York Times DealBook Summit, Chip Dispatch reported on November 20, 2026. Musk called it “an autonomous version of the Model Y that won’t have steering wheels or pedals,” according to Electrek, and said it would be “good for transporting groups of 6 or 7 people.” He gave no launch date, price or production site. It would join Tesla’s Model Y Robotaxis, which keep conventional controls, and the two-seat Cybercab, which opened public rides in Dallas on November 19, its second city after Austin. Personal Cybercab orders are priced at $29,990 with a required $299-a-month subscription. Chip Dispatch notes federal safety standards are written around a human driver, and NHTSA issued a Special Order over the Cybercab in September, so permission to operate without a driver remains the gating item.

title: Superhuman pushes its Go assistant into Docs, Mail and 20 new connected agents
summary: Superhuman, the company formerly known as Grammarly, is rolling out a more personalized Go assistant that learns context across apps, makes agents available in Docs and adds third-party agent integrations, TechCrunch reported on November 19, 2026. Go works inline with the cursor, manages other agents and is becoming proactive, watching your schedule and email and drafting replies in your own writing style. The company is adding 20 new connected agents through its Go SDK, including DeepL, Legora, Amplitude, Databricks and Blackboard. In Docs, Go agents can run tasks in the background and users can set routines to trigger workflows, while Go is replacing the AI tools at the center of Superhuman Mail. CEO Shishir Mehrotra said Go has over 1 million active users. “Go is definitely more work-focused than some of the tools coming out of the pure consumer ecosystem,” he told TechCrunch.

title: Voyager 1 passes one light-day from Earth, and the Empire State Building glows gold
summary: The Empire State Building was lit gold this week to celebrate NASA’s Voyager 1 passing one light-day from Earth, Good News Network reported on November 19, 2026. On Wednesday the spacecraft reached the distance light travels in 24 hours, about 16 billion miles, so a signal now takes a full day to get home. “The color gold is emblematic of the gold-plated copper phonograph record that is flying on Voyager,” NASA wrote. The record carries 115 images, natural sounds, music and spoken greetings in 55 languages. Launched in 1977, Voyager 1 crossed into interstellar space in 2012. True to form, it marked the occasion with a hiccup: on Tuesday it stopped sending science and engineering data, though its carrier signal was still found. “We never know for sure what’s going to happen with the Voyagers, but it constantly amazes me when they just keep going,” project manager Suzanne Dodd told CNN in 2024.

title: She checked on her ‘loud’ upstairs neighbor, and strangers raised more than $109,000
summary: When Heidi Widmer moved to Culver City, she was losing sleep over a thumping upstairs neighbor, Good News Network reported on November 19, 2026. Then she met Carole, an 87-year-old with Parkinson’s disease who had taken about 20 minutes to get down the stairs with a walker. “Am I too loud for you?” Carole asked. “That was just such a humbling moment for me,” Widmer said. She now takes out Carole’s trash, cooks for her once a week and got the landlord to replace a broken fridge and stove. After her posts drew nearly 30 million views, a GoFundMe titled “Help Carole Live With Comfort & Dignity” raised more than $109,000, with plans for a stair lift so Carole can stay in her home. “Now I got a grandma,” Widmer said. Her advice: “Lead with curiosity and kindness.”

title: Teens can drop in for console gaming at the Main Library this afternoon
summary: The Lafayette Public Library hosts Drop-in Gaming on Friday, November 20, 2026, from 3:30 to 5 p.m. in the Teen Area of the Main Library downtown, according to the library’s event listing. The program invites teens to “join old and new friends to play on various gaming consoles.” It is for ages 12 to 18, and the listing describes it as an in-person program in the Teen Area. The listing shows more Friday sessions on December 4, 11 and 18, so teens who miss this afternoon can catch the next round after Thanksgiving. It’s an easy way for teens to end the school week with friends, and the library’s calendar shows other teen programs that week, including Teen Winter Games on Monday evening.

title: ‘Stars’ takes Science Museum planetarium visitors to the far reaches of the galaxy Sunday
summary: The University of Louisiana at Lafayette Science Museum shows the planetarium program Stars on Sunday, November 22, 2026, from 2:45 to 3:15 p.m., according to the museum’s event listing. “Every star has a story,” the listing says. “Some are as old as time, faint and almost forgotten. Others burn bright and end their lives in powerful explosions.” The show promises a journey “to the farthest reaches of our galaxy” to experience both the beauty and destructive power of stars. Produced by Sudekum Planetarium and NSC Creative, it runs 26 minutes and is best for ages 10 and up. The museum’s calendar also notes it will be closed November 26 and 27 for the Thanksgiving holiday.

title: Santa Claus is coming to the South Regional Library on Monday
summary: Santa Claus visits the Lafayette Public Library’s South Regional Library on Monday, November 23, 2026, from 10 a.m. to noon in the Story Time Room, according to the library’s event listing. “Come visit Santa Claus at the library!” the listing says. Children can take a picture with Santa using a parent’s own phone, then stay for a craft. The visit is for ages 0 to 18, and families are welcome. The library’s calendar shows Santa making more stops that week, including the West Regional Library from 1 to 2 p.m. the same Monday and the Main Library on Tuesday morning, so families can pick the branch that fits their schedule.

title: Teens compete for gold at the Main Library’s Teen Winter Games Monday night
summary: The Lafayette Public Library’s Main Library hosts Teen Winter Games on Monday, November 23, 2026, from 6 to 7:30 p.m. in the Teen Area, according to the library’s event listing. “We’re taking over the teen department for the Teen Library Winter Games indoor challenge,” the listing says. Teens can “test your skills, compete for prizes in a variety of games, and have the chance to take home the Gold.” The program is for ages 12 to 18. The library’s calendar lists the event under its Main Library teen programs, alongside Friday afternoon Drop-in Gaming sessions for the same age group.

title: CHB Lafayette’s Book du Mois discusses Louise Erdrich’s ‘The Sentence’ Tuesday
summary: CHB Lafayette’s monthly book club, Book du Mois, meets at 6:15 p.m. on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, at the bookstore at 302A Jefferson St. downtown to discuss The Sentence by Louise Erdrich, according to Downtown Lafayette’s event listing. The novel follows a small independent bookstore in Minneapolis that is haunted from November 2019 to November 2020 by “the store’s most annoying customer,” Flora, who dies on All Souls’ Day but “simply won’t leave the store.” A CHB bookseller leads the discussion, and members vote at meetings on upcoming monthly picks. Readers can “pop by the bookshop to get your copy, or order online,” the listing says.

title: Overstuffed Trivia Night brings five rounds to the Legends Annex patio the night before Thanksgiving
summary: Legends Annex at 110 Polk St. hosts Overstuffed Trivia Night on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, from 7 to 8:30 p.m., according to Downtown Lafayette’s event listing. The evening offers “FIVE rounds of general knowledge trivia” on the Legends Annex patio, or indoors “if the weather is not agreeable.” Teams can have up to 8 players, and the listing pitches it as a way to spend the night before Thanksgiving with visiting family or friends. “Trivia starts at 7pm sharp,” the listing warns, so teams should arrive early. Metered street parking downtown is free after 5 p.m. on weekdays, Downtown Lafayette notes.
